definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord's manifestations: the pre-eminent member of each class, named 'by the chief ones' (10.19–39), endless and given only by way of indication (10.40); whatever being has vibhūti, glory or vigour springs from a portion of his splendour (10.41). Knowing his vibhūti and yoga in truth joins one to unwavering yoga (10.7); Arjuna asks for them as supports for contemplating him (10.16–18).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Said of the Lord's own power: 'my vibhūti and yoga' (10.7, 10.18), 'my sovereign yoga' seen with the divine eye (11.8), the supreme form shown 'by my own yoga' (11.47); he is addressed as yogin (10.17) and lord of yoga (11.4, 11.9). Said also of the devotee's discipline: 'unwavering yoga' (10.7), 'yoga directed to nothing else' (12.6), 'the yoga of practice' (12.9); 'resorting to my yoga' (12.11).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna addresses the Lord as viśvarūpa on seeing him with many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes, endless in form on every side, without end, middle or beginning (11.16); he later calls him viśvamūrti, 'whose body is the universe' (11.46). The form is 'universal, endless, primal', shown by the Lord's grace and own yoga (11.47).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The eye the Lord gives Arjuna because he cannot see him with his own eye; with it he is to behold the Lord's sovereign yoga (11.8).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: An epithet of the Lord seen in the universal form: 'the imperishable, the highest, to be known' (11.18) and 'the imperishable: being and non-being and what is beyond' (11.37). In 12.1 and 12.3 'the imperishable, the unmanifest' is named as the object of a worship distinct from worshipping the Lord in the manner of 11.55; it is described as indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, fixed (12.3). In 10.25 and 10.33 akṣara means 'syllable' and 'letter'.

notes: The referent of akṣara in 12.1–3 is disputed among the commentators (see dsp:bhagavad-gita-manifest-or-unmanifest-worship).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'The imperishable, the unmanifest' worshipped by some (12.1, 12.3); for those whose cetas is attached to the unmanifest the hardship is greater, since the unmanifest goal is reached with pain by the embodied (12.5).

literal: standing on the peak / like an anvil; unchanging

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: One of the epithets of the imperishable worshipped by some (12.3).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Epithet of the imperishable worshipped by some: unthinkable (12.3).

literal: not to be pointed out; indefinable

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: First epithet of the imperishable worshipped by some: that which cannot be indicated or defined (12.3).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Epithet of the imperishable worshipped by some: all-pervading (12.3).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: By devotion directed to nothing else (bhaktyā ananyayā) alone the Lord in this form can be known, seen in truth and entered (11.54); cf. worship 'with yoga directed to nothing else' (ananyena yogena, 12.6).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The means for one unable to fix citta steadily on the Lord: seek to reach him by the yoga of practice (12.9).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The yoga of practice for one who cannot fix citta steadily (12.9); one unable even in practice should be intent on work for the Lord (12.10); knowledge is said to be better than practice (12.12).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: For one unable even to work for the Lord: resorting to his yoga, self-restrained, relinquish the fruit of all actions (12.11); it is ranked above meditation, and from relinquishment peace follows immediately (12.12).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotees who worship the Lord ever joined (12.1); 'my devotee' (madbhakta) who does his work and holds him highest comes to him (11.55); the devotee 'full of devotion' (bhaktimat) with the marks of 12.13–19 is dear to him; those who follow the nectar of dharma with faith are exceedingly dear (12.20).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The wise, understanding the Lord as the source of all, worship (bhajante) him with bhāva (10.8); he gives buddhiyoga to those who worship with love (10.10); by devotion directed to nothing else he can be known, seen in truth and entered (11.54).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Given by the Lord to those ever joined who worship him with love, as that by which they come to him (10.10).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: First of the states of beings that arise from the Lord (10.4); the devotee is to let buddhi enter the Lord (12.8) and has manas and buddhi offered to him (12.14). Named alongside, and distinct from, manas.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Among the senses the Lord is manas (10.22); those who fix manas on him are the most joined (12.2); 'place your manas in me alone' (12.8); manas and buddhi offered to the Lord (12.14); Arjuna's manas is shaken with fear at the terrible form (11.45) and is to become glad (11.49).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Devotees have their citta on the Lord (maccitta, 10.9); if one cannot fix citta steadily in him, one should seek him by the yoga of practice (12.9).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The hardship is greater for those whose cetas is attached to the unmanifest (12.5); the Lord lifts before long those whose cetas has entered him (12.7); after the vision Arjuna says he is 'sacetāḥ', with cetas regained (11.51). Used alongside but distinct from manas, citta and buddhi.
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'In beings I am cetanā' (10.22): the awareness of living beings is one of the Lord's manifestations.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of those that reckon (or impel) I am time' (10.30); 'I alone am imperishable time' (10.33); 'I am Time, grown mighty, the maker of the destruction of worlds, engaged in drawing in the worlds' (11.32); the Lord's mouths are like the fire of time (kālānala, 11.25).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: What Arjuna is told to be: the warriors are already slain by the Lord as Time; 'be merely the instrument (or occasion), left-handed archer' (11.33).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of the sciences I am the knowledge concerning the self' (10.32).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord's teaching is called 'the supreme secret named adhyātma', by which Arjuna's delusion is gone (11.1); 'of sciences, adhyātma-vidyā' (10.32).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of recitation' (10.25).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of utterances I am the single syllable (ekam akṣaram)' (10.25) — the syllable identified in 8.13 as 'om, the one-syllabled brahman'.

notes: 10.25 does not itself say 'oṃ'; the identification rests on 8.13.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna repeatedly asks the Lord to 'be gracious' (prasīda, 11.25, 11.31, 11.45) and seeks his grace by prostration (prasādaye, 11.44); the Lord says he showed the supreme form 'being gracious' (prasanna) to him (11.47).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna's address to the Lord, who alone knows himself by himself (10.15), and whose sovereign form he asks to see (11.3).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna calls the Lord the supreme brahman and supreme abode (10.12), and the knower, the known and the supreme abode (11.38).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of secret things I am silence' (10.38); the devotee dear to the Lord is silent (maunin, 12.19).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: A mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: A mark of the devotee dear to the Lord, named together with nirmama (12.13).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Evenness (samatā) is among the states that arise from the Lord (10.5); worshippers of the imperishable are even-minded (samabuddhi) everywhere (12.4); the dear devotee is the same in pain and pleasure (12.13), to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, cold and heat, and holds blame and praise equal (12.18–19).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord is friendly (maitra) and compassionate toward beings, hating none (12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord is compassionate (karuṇa) (12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Among the states that arise from the Lord (10.4) and among the feminine things he is (10.34); the dear devotee is forbearing (kṣamin, 12.13).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The dear devotee is ever content (santuṣṭa, 12.14) and content with whatever comes (12.19); contentment (tuṣṭi) is among the states that arise from the Lord (10.5).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: A mark of the devotee dear to the Lord: unconcerned, taking no side (12.16).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: A mark of the devotee dear to the Lord: without a fixed abode (12.19).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Those who worship the Lord endowed with supreme faith are held the most joined (12.2); those who follow the nectar of dharma with faith (śraddadhāna) are exceedingly dear (12.20).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Two kinds of worship (upāsate, paryupāsate) are contrasted: of the Lord by devotees ever joined (12.1–2, 12.6) and of the imperishable unmanifest (12.1, 12.3); those who attend to (paryupāsate) the nectar of dharma are exceedingly dear (12.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The greater hardship of those whose cetas is attached to the unmanifest (12.5) — used here in the general sense of toil, not the technical list of afflictions.

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: One who holds the Lord as highest (matparama) and does his work comes to him (11.55); those intent on him renounce all actions in him (12.6); those who follow the nectar of dharma holding him highest are exceedingly dear (12.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva' (10.37); the narrator calls Kṛṣṇa Vāsudeva when he resumes his own form (11.50).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Every being with glory springs from a portion of the Lord's splendour (tejo'ṃśa, 10.41); he stands supporting the whole world with a single portion (ekāṃśa, 10.42).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'I am the splendour of the splendid' (10.36); whatever is glorious springs from a portion of the Lord's splendour (10.41); the universal form is a mass of splendour that heats and fills the world (11.17, 11.19, 11.30) and is 'made of splendour' (11.47).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The darkness born of ignorance, which the Lord, out of compassion, destroys in his devotees with the shining lamp of knowledge (10.11).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Doing actions for the Lord's sake one attains perfection (12.10).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: From relinquishment of the fruit of actions, peace follows immediately (12.12).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Devotees who renounce all actions in the Lord worship him meditating (dhyāyantaḥ) with undivided yoga (12.6); meditation is superior to knowledge, and relinquishment of fruits superior to meditation (12.12).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Among the states that arise from the Lord (10.4); the shining lamp of knowledge with which he destroys the darkness of ignorance (10.11); 'of knowers I am knowledge' (10.38); knowledge is better than practice, meditation superior to knowledge (12.12).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of secret things I am silence' (10.38); the teaching named adhyātma is 'the supreme secret' (11.1).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna says: 'you are the imperishable: being and non-being (sad asat), and that which is beyond' (11.37).

notes: Construed either as 'being, non-being and what is beyond' or 'the imperishable beyond being and non-being'.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord gives buddhiyoga to those ever joined (satatayukta, 10.10); Arjuna asks about devotees ever joined (12.1); those who worship him ever joined (nityayukta) with supreme faith are held the most joined (yuktatama, 12.2).

literal: one who gives up all undertakings

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: A mark of the devotee dear to the Lord (12.16).
Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: A mark of the devotee dear to the Lord: without expectation (12.16).
